say.f: Days very likely warmer than average to January; unusually hot days most likely in Victoria; November drier on the coast.
say.m: A strong El Niño into autumn: warmer than average, rain near normal.
say.p: No outlook issued yet. Drought and canopy loss carry on after the heat.

windows.why: Hot days arrive as flying-fox pups are born and birds are nesting.
Rain fails as flowering peaks: less nectar for bees, birds and bats.
Unusually warm nights leave no cool hours to recover in.
Soil and ponds dry out; old trees shed limbs and the canopy thins.

src: BoM long-range forecast, Nov 2026–Jan 2027 (15 Oct): above-average highs over 80% likely; unusually hot days over 70% in parts of Victoria
BoM ENSO update: Niño 3.4 +2.81 °C in the week to 11 Oct 2026, near record, strengthening through spring; positive IOD likely
WMO: Niño 3.4 near +3.7 °C for Oct–Dec 2026, peaking around December (8 Oct)
NOAA CPC: strong to very strong El Niño likely through Jan–Mar 2027 (13 Oct)
ABC: November drier on the coast from Adelaide to Melbourne; no clear summer rain signal (17 Oct)
Agriculture Victoria: warmer Jan–Mar 2027, rain near neutral
